collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A hillside stripped by careless harvesting is washing away: start a long replanting effort, or let it heal on its own.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The hillside above the village was stripped of its bushes for firewood years ago, and now every rain washes mud into the gardens. (subject) wants a long effort: plant the slope, terrace it, guard it for years. (friend) says nature heals itself, given time. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: Every family plants ten bushes a season on the slope. Many die. Some live. After five years, the mud has slowed. After ten, the hillside is green. Nobody who started it is young anymore.

text_only.reason: a death only talked about (or the word's everyday sense); nobody dies -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village leaves the slope alone. It heals, very slowly, while the gardens keep filling with mud. After a few years, (friend) admits nature could use a hand, and the planting begins.
